title: Etiquette & language
body:
Catalan is Andorra's sole official language — Andorra is the only country in the world where it holds that status — but the country is thoroughly multilingual: Spanish is the most widely spoken second language, with French and Portuguese also common because of immigration patterns. A 2022 survey put Catalan as the habitual language for about 64% of residents and Spanish for about 49% (respondents could name more than one) — the mix reflects immigration and cross-border tourism rather than a shift away from Catalan. Menus and signage in the capital regularly run in three or four languages, but English coverage thins out once you're off Avinguda Meritxell.

A few Catalan basics go a long way: hola (hello), si us plau (please), gràcies (thank you), adéu (goodbye). Since most residents default to Spanish or French with visitors, leading with either — plus a Catalan hola and gràcies — reads as more considered than English alone.

Andorra is a small, conservative Pyrenean country: casual dress is fine everywhere except church interiors (Sant Esteve, Casa de la Vall's chapel), where covering shoulders is appreciated.
